item.title: Ukrainian woman designing a ballistic missile to put Moscow in reach
item.description: Before Russia invaded, Iryna Terekh designed patios. Now she runs a Ukrainian defense company testing a missile she says will soon put Moscow in range.

item.title: The millennial woman building Ukraine's ballistic missile
item.description: Iryna Terekh was an architect designing patios across Ukraine when her life changed. Now she runs Fire Point, a defense company testing a new ballistic missile intended to reach Moscow. CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Lithuania training civilians to defend against a Russian invasion
item.description: Lithuania is teaching civilians young and old to help defend their tiny nation from a hypothetical Russian invasion, and telling Putin, "We don't fear you."

item.title: King Charles breaks silence on Harry and Meghan's U.K. return
item.description: King Charles III clarified in a letter sent to senior government officials that Prince Harry and his wife Meghan are nonworking royals after their move back to the United Kingdom. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect
item.description: Canada's retaliatory tariffs against the U.S. took effect early Tuesday morning, impacting goods like milk, perfume and golf clubs as the trade war between the countries drags on. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Baltic nations brace for possible Russian attacks
item.description: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are preparing to become Russia's next target amid its ongoing war with Ukraine. Aaron MacLean reports.

item.title: Lithuania prepares for potential war with Russia
item.description: Lithuanian citizens are preparing for potential Russian aggression as the Ukraine war rages on. CBS News' Aaron MacLean reports.

item.title: Price of crude oil nears $100 a barrel as U.S.-Iran stalemate continues
item.description: Oil prices are rising steadily with no end in sight to the U.S.-Iran standoff impeding tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Key questions surrounding the deadly Amazon Air plane crash in Miami
item.description: An Amazon Air cargo plane overran the runway while landing in Miami, hitting two vehicles and killing five people. Capt. Laura Einsetler, a commercial airline pilot, shares her thoughts about the upcoming investigation.

item.title: Amazon plane crash victims were all in vehicles hit by aircraft, NTSB says
item.description: The National Transportation Safety Board shared more details on the Amazon cargo plane crash at the Miami International Airport that killed at least five people and injured several more. All of the victims of the crash were in cars hit by the aircraft, the NTSB said. Skyler Henry has the latest.

item.title: Expert reacts as Trump tries to downplay the Iran war
item.description: The Iran war continues as the midterm general election approaches and as President Trump downplays the conflict. Retired Vice Admiral Robert B. Murrett weighs in.

item.title: Patrick Clancy's lawyer threatens conspiracy theorists with legal action
item.description: Patrick Clancy, Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband, issued a scathing statement to conspiracy theorists who have been claiming he was involved in the deaths of the couple's children - "There will be consequences."

item.title: Amazon cargo plane crash victims were in vehicles that were hit, NTSB says
item.description: An Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway at Miami International Airport and crashed into two vehicles before coming to a stop and bursting into flames. Five people were killed.

item.title: France investigates removal of female Eiffel Tower staff for Hindu group's visit
item.description: The mayor of Paris announced an investigation into why female staff at the Eiffel Tower were taken off duty for a visit from a Hindu religious group.

item.title: What to expect from the first-ever Republican midterm convention
item.description: Republicans will gather in Dallas, Texas, for their first-ever midterm convention. President Trump and Vice President JD Vance will headline the event. CBS News' Shawna Mizelle has more.

item.title: Canada hits back in Trump's trade war with heavy export tariffs
item.description: A set of U.S. exports to Canada face heavy tariffs in retaliation for President Trump's levies on Canadian goods. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: An iconic photo of the new 60 Minutes team in Murrow's old hangout
item.description: Famed photographer Mark Seliger captured the season 59 team at New York City's Oyster Bar in Grand Central Station.

item.title: First on 60 Minutes: U.S. Air Force officer shot down in Iran details his rescue
item.description: The weapons system officer was part of the two-man crew shot down over Iran, prompting one of the most complex rescue operations in U.S. military history.

item.title: U.S. Air Force officer rescued from Iran speaks for the first time to 60 Minutes
item.description: After a U.S. warplane was shot down over Iran, the Air Force and American special forces rescued the two-man crew in one of the largest and most complex rescue operations in U.S. military history. For the 59th season premiere of 60 Minutes, correspondent Norah O'Donnell interviews the weapon systems officer who spent two days on the ground in Iran. In his first public account of what happened, the colonel describes surviving a harrowing ejection and being injured, how he evaded Iranian forces and what he said to his rescuers when they arrived.

item.title: Small plane goes missing off Bahamas carrying 4 members of Florida family
item.description: A small plane carrying four family members flying back home to Florida went missing off the Bahamas, the U.S. Coast Guard and authorities in the Bahamas said.

item.title: Dangerous Hurricane Lowell passing just west of Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lowell was skirting western Hawaii, bringing damaging winds, heavy rain and punishing waves, the National Hurricane Center said.

item.title: Jill Is Rooting for a Crash?! | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: You heard that right: Jill is rooting for a market crash. In today's episode, Certified Financial Planner Kayla Sabbagh joins Jill and Mark to explain why Jill might be onto something—and how, in some cases, a market crash can be good for your wallet. Plus, Jill and the gang help caller Jessica make a financial plan for her move across the country.

item.title: Ross Fire still burning, with over 90,000 acres scorched
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: 2 paintings by Renoir stolen from museum in France, officials say
item.description: Authorities are seeking thieves who broke into the Renoir Museum in the French Riviera and stole two paintings by the impressionist master, local authorities say.

item.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv resume as soon as Witkoff, Kushner peace talks end
item.description: Russian strikes pummeled Ukraine's capital as soon as a three-day pause for peace talks with President Trump's envoys ended.

item.title: N.H. voters choose nominees for open Senate seat, and more races to watch today
item.description: Both Democrats and Republicans are targeting the Senate seat that will be vacated by Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, who is not running for reelection.

item.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods take effect
item.description: Canada's steep retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods took effect just after midnight ET on Tuesday, deepening the trade war between the two countries.

item.title: Hurricane warning issued for western Hawaii as Lowell approaches
item.description: The National Hurricane Center posted a hurricane warning for western Hawaii's Kauai County as Hurricane Lowell moved toward the area as a Category 2 storm.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11, Taliban rules Afghanistan again, but with U.S. firepower
item.description: CBS News finds Taliban forces patrolling Kabul in American armored vehicles, wearing American tactical gear and carrying American weapons.

item.title: Mom found guilty of abuse for letting 5-year-old walk outside alone
item.description: "We just expected that as soon as this gets in front of a prosecutor actually looking at it and a judge, this is all gonna go away," Karyann Parkinson said.
